name: Doncaster
location: The southerly portion of the township of Doncaster, in the county of Montcalm.
tribe_band: Iroquois of Sault St. Louis and Lake of Two Mountains.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Maniwaki
location: At the confluence of the Desert river with the Gatineau river, in the county of Ottawa
tribe_band: Algonquins of the Lake of Two Mountains.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Temiscaming
location: At the head of Lake Temiscaming in the county of Pontiac.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Whitworth
location: Lots 27, 28 and 29, concession 12, township of Whitworth, county of Temiscouata.
tribe_band: Amalecites of Isle Verte, and Viger.
remarks: Purchased by the Department of Indian Affairs, March 31, 1877.

name: Cacouna
location: Lot No. 66, shown on the cadastral plan of the village of Cacouna, county of Temiscouata.
tribe_band: Amalecites of Isle Verte and Viger.
remarks: Purchased by the Department of Indian Affairs, July 8, 1891.

name: Weymontaching
location: On the north side of the St. Maurice river, opposite the mouth of the Manouan river, county of Champlain.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Coucoucache
location: On the north side of the St. Maurice river, opposite the mouth of the outlet from Lake Coucoucache, county de Champlain.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions, of the Act 14 and 15 Vic., chap. 106. (See No. 1.)

name: Escoumains
location: Near the mouth of the Escoumains river, township of Escoumains, county of Saguenay.
remarks: Purchased in 1892 by the Department of Indian Affairs.

name: Maganettawan
remarks: Reserved under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty, September 9, 1850; subsequently surveyed and confirmed by O.C., January 31, 1853.

name: Henvey Inlet
location: At Henvey Inlet on Georgian bay.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Point Grondin
location: At Point Grondin, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Whitefish River
location: At the mouth of Whitefish river, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Spanish River
location: At the mouth of Spanish river, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Whitefish Lake
location: At Whitefish lake, about 16 miles north of Collins Inlet, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty. The reserve was not surveyed until 1884. The boundaries as then surveyed were amended and established by judgment of the court of January 21, 1889. (Attorney General of Ontario vs Francis et al.)

name: Serpent River
location: The peninsula east of the mouth of Serpent river, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Mississagua River
location: At the mouth of Mississagua river, north shore of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Dokis
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. See note to No. 1.)

name: Nipissing
location: On the north shore of Lake Nipissing
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Wanapitae
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Robinson Huron Treaty. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Thessalon
location: At the southeast corner of the township of Thessalon, north of Lake Huron.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. The reserve originally consisted of the entire township, all of which except the present reserve, has been surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians. (See note to No. 1.

name: French River
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Garden River
location: At Garden river, near Sault Ste. marie
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. The reserve originally consisted of a tract containing about 130,000 acres, all of which, except the present reserve, has been surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Goulais Bay
location: At Batchewaung bay, east end of Lake Superior.
remarks: The original reserve contained about 157,440 acres, was set apart under the Robinson Huron Treaty, subsequently surveyed and finally confirmed by O.C., January 31, 1852. It was surrendered for sale, for the benefit of the Indians, in 1859. The present reserve at Goulais bay is a portion of the original reserve set apart by Orders in Council in 1879 and 1885.

name: Whitefish Island
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. Part of the 15th reservation.

name: Parry Island
location: In Georgian bay, near its eastern shore
remarks: Under the provisions of the Robinson-Huron Treaty the reserve was located on the mainland. The island was surveyed in lieu of that location, and the survey approved by the Commissioner of Crown Lands November 22, 1853.

name: Shawanaga
location: In the township of Shawanaga, parry Sound district.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

name: Naiscoutaing
location: In the townships of Wallbridge and Harrison, Parry Sound district.
remarks: Robinson Huron Treaty. (See note to No. 1.)

location: Lots 34 and 35, concession 7, township of Shawanaga, Parry Sound district.
tribe_band: Shawanaga Band of Ojibewas of Lake Huron.
remarks: Vested by Order in Council of the Provincial Government dated December 31, 1877, in the Dominion Government in trust for the Shawanaga band of Indians so long as the said band continues to occupy the said lots.

name: Temogaming
tribe_band: A band of Ojibewas of Lake Huron, who had not been provided with a reserve under the provisions of the Robinson-Huron Treaty.
remarks: Surveyed in 1884. This reserve has not been confirmed by the Provincial Government of Ontario.

name: Cockburn Island
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.
remarks: The Manitoulin islands and islands on the north shore of Lake Huron were set apart, August 9, 1836, by Sir Edmund Head, as a reserve for the Ottawas and Chippewas, and any other Indians who should be allowed to settle thereon. The Manitoulin and adjacent islands were surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians October 6, 1862, and under the provisions of this surrender the present reserves, numbered 19 to 26 inclusive, were set apart.

name: Sheshegwaning
location: In the Tp. of Robinson, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Obidgewong
location: In the Tps. of Mills and Burpee, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: West Bay
location: In the Tp. of Billings, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Sucker Creek
location: In the Tp. of Howland, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Sheguiandah
location: In the Tp. of Sheguiandah, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Sucker Lake
location: In the Tp. of Assiginack, Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Manitoulin Island (unceded portion).
location: The eastern peninsula of Manitoulin island.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Cape Croker
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.
remarks: The Saugeen peninsula was set apart as an Indian reserve August 9, 1836, by Sir Edmund Head, and surrendered for sale for the benefit of the Indians, October 13, 1854. Reserves Nos. 27, 28 and 29 were set apart under the provisions of the said surrender of October 13, 1854.

name: Chief's Point
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Saugeen Reserve
location: southwestern corner of the Saugeen peninsula.
tribe_band: Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Hunting Reserve
location: In the township of St. Edmund
tribe_band: Chippewas of Saugeen and Cape Croker.
remarks: Set apart from unsold Indian lands by Order in Council of November 19, 1896, as hunting grounds for the Chippewa bands of Saugeen and Cape Croker. F. 160,542.
The islands in Lake Huron claimed by these Indians were ceded in error in 1850 by the Ottawas and Chippewas of Lake Huron.

name: Christian Islands, viz:- Christian, Hope and Beckwith.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Lake Couchiching, Simcoe and Huron.
remarks: These islands were reserved in the surrender made by these Indians, June 5, 1856, of the islands situated in Lake Huron which they claimed.

name: Gibson or Watha
location: The eastern portion of the township of Gibson, county of Muskoka.
remarks: Purchased from the Provincial Government in 1881 for such members of the Oka band of Indians as might desire to settle there.

name: Rama
location: In the township of Rama, county of Ontario.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Lakes Couchiching, Simcoe and Huron.
remarks: Purchased from private parties at different dates between 1843 and 1848.

name: Georgina Island
location: Georgina, Snake and Fox islands in Lake Simcoe, and other islands in Lake Couchiching.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Lakes Couchiching, Simcoe and Huron.
remarks: These islands have remained in the possession of the Indians, and have never been ceded by them by treaty or purchase.

name: Scugog
location: On the island in Lake Scugog
remarks: Purchased by these Indians with the proceeds of their own annuities, November 3, 1843.

name: Mud Lake
location: On Mud lake, in the township of Smith, county of Peterborough
remarks: Granted in 1837 to the New England Company. Transferred to the Dominion Government in trust for the Indians, October 12, 1898, less a portion containing 115 64 acres reserved by the company.

name: Rice Lake
location: On the north share of Rice lake, in the county of Peterborough
remarks: 1,120 acres of this reserve was granted in 1834 to trustees, for the benefit of Indian tribes in the province. The remainder of the reserve was purchased by the Indians with their own funds.

name: Islands in the Trent waters
location: In the counties of Peterborough and Victoria.
tribe_band: Mississaguas of Rice, Mud and Scugog lakes
remarks: Claimed by these Indians not to have been included in treaty of 1818, and claim subsequently admitted by the Crown Lands Department.

name: Alnwick
location: In the township of Alnwick, county of Northumberland.
remarks: Purchased from private owners at different dates between 1836 and 1870.

name: Sugar Island
location: In Rice lake, in front of the 4th and 5th concessions of Otonabee.
remarks: Purchased for the Alnwick Indians by deed from Win. Kempt, dated January 13, 1899, for $775, from their funds.

name: Tyendinaga
location: On the bay of Quinte - The southern part of the township of Tyendinaga.
tribe_band: Mohawks of the bay of Quinte
remarks: The reserve consisted originally of 92,700 acres granted under letters patent from the Crown in 1793, all of which, except the present reserve, has been surrendered and sold and the proceeds applied for the benefit of the Indians. Salmon island and marshes were added by O.C. November 13, 1900. F. 78,703.

name: Golden Lake
location: At the southern end of Golden lake, in the county of Peterborough.
remarks: Purchased by the Dominion Government from the Provincial Government of Ontario in 1870 as a reserve for these Indians.

name: Tuscarora
location: The township of Tuscarora and parts of the townships of Oneida and Onondaga.
tribe_band: The Six Nations, consisting of the Mohawks, Oneidas, Onondagas, Tuscaroras, Cayugas, Senecas and Delawares.
remarks: A tract six miles wide on each side of the Grand river, was granted to the Six Nations in 1784 by Sir F. Haldimand, containing about 694,910 acres. This grant was confirmed to them by letters patent in 1793 by Governor Simcoe. All of the tract, except the present reserve, has been surrendered in portions from time to time and sold for the benefit of the Indians. In 1847 the Six Nations invited the Mississaguas of the Credit to settle on their reserve, and offered them a free grant of 6,000 acres for the purpose. A number accepted, who now reside in the southwest corner of the reserve.

name: Oneida
location: In the township of Delaware, county of Middlesex.
remarks: Purchased for these Indians by the Government in 1840 with their own money which they brought with them from the United States.

name: Caradoc
location: In the township of Caradoc, county of Middlesex.
tribe_band: Chippewas of the Thames and Munsees.
remarks: Reserved by the Chippewas in the cession made by them of the 'Longwood Tract' in 1819. A small portion of the reservation was surrendered in 1834 and sold for the benefit of the Indians.

name: Stony Point or Aux Sables
location: In the township of Bosanquet, county of Lambton.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Chenail, Ecarté and St. Clair.
remarks: Reserved by these Indians in the cession of a large tract in the London and Western districts made by them in 1827.

name: Kettle Point
location: In the township of Bosanquet, county of Lambton.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Chenail, Ecarté and St. Clair.
remarks: Reserved by these Indians in the cession of a large tract in the London and Western districts made by them in 1827.

name: Sarnia
location: In the township of Sarnia, county of Lambton.
tribe_band: Chippewas of Chenail, Ecarté and St. Clair.
remarks: Reserved by these Indians in the cession of a large tract in the London and Western districts made by them in 1827.

name: Walpole Island
location: At the head of Lake St. Clair.
tribe_band: Chippewas and Pottawattamies of Walpole Island.
remarks: The Chippewas settled on the island in 1831 by order of the Government. The island appears to have been then set apart by the Government as a Crown reserve to be used for the purpose of settling Indians thereon. The Pottawattamies came from the United States in 1841, and, on petition, were permitted by the Government to settle on the island.

name: Orford
location: In the township of Orford, county of Kent.
remarks: The reserve originally consisted of 51,160 acres situated in the townships of Zone and Orford, and was set apart by Order in Council in 1793. All the reservation, except the present reserve, has been surrendered and sold for the benefit of the Indians.

name: Michipicoten
location: On the Michipicoten river, about one mile from its mouth.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians who resided on the land. This reserve has not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Gros Cap
location: On the north shore of Lake Superior, about a mile west of Michipicoten river.
remarks: Set apart in accordance with the, provisions of the Robinson Superior Treaty.

name: Pic River
location: On the Pic river, near its mouth
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians who resided on the land. These reserves have not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Pays Plat
location: At Pays Plat, north shore of Lake Superior.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians who resided on the land. These reserves have not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Fort William
location: Near the west end of Lake Superior
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Robinson Superior Treaty.

name: Red Rock
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians who resided on the land. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: McIntyre Bay
location: On the south shore of Lake Nipigon
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians of Lake Nipigon. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Gull River
location: At the mouth of Gull river, on the west shore of Lake Nipigon.
remarks: Set apart under the provisions of the Robinson Superior Treaty. Surveyed in 1887. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Island Point
location: On the west shore of Lake Nipigon
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians of Lake Nipigon. These reserves have not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Jackfish Island
location: A small island near the west shore of Lake Nipigon.
remarks: Surveyed in 1885 for the Indians of Lake Nipigon. These reserves have not been confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Long Lake
location: At the north end of Long lake
remarks: Surveyed in 1881; for the Indians residing on the land. Not confirmed by the Provincial Government.

name: Cornwall Island
location: In the River St. Lawrence near the boundary between Ontario and Quebec
remarks: This and adjacent islands form part of the reserve of these Indians held by them from the time French rule began in this country.

name: Saugeen Indians Hunting Ground
location: Lots 11 to 20, inclusive, in concessions III and IV; lots 11 to 18 and lot 20 in concessions I and II, all east of the Bury road, township of St. Edmund, county of Bruce.
remarks: Set apart by Order in Council of November 16, 1896. Lots 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 18 and 20 in concessions I and II, E.B.R., are set apart for the Saugeen reserve Indians, and lots 11 to 20, inclusive, in concessions III and IV, E.B.R., for the Cape Croker band.

name: Buffalo Point
location: Lake of the Woods, in Manitoba.

name: Big Island
location: Lake of the Woods, in Manitoba.

name: Lake of the Woods
location: Certain islands in Lake of the Woods.

name: St. Peters
location: St. Andrew's and St. Clement's, Manitoba.

name: Long Plain, Assiniboine River
location: Portage la Prairie and South Norfolk, Man.
